title: Maelstrom — Chrome Obsession and Red Multi-Optic Visors
content: Born from the old Metal Warriors, Maelstrom operates out of Northside industrial warehouses like All Foods and their heavy-metal club, Totentanz. They despise organic flesh, ripping away parts of their own faces to install red multi-optic arrays and stolen military hardware that keeps them teetering on the edge of cyberpsychosis.

title: Maelstrom Infighting: Brick, Simon Royce, and Dum Dum
content: Maelstrom has been fractured ever since the psycho Simon Royce betrayed and locked away their previous leader, Brick (who was far more pragmatic about business deals), behind a laser tripwire mine. Royce and his right-hand man Dum Dum tore up past deals with Militech and stoked extreme paranoia; if Brick survives and is rescued, he retakes Totentanz.

title: Tyger Claws — Cyber-Yakuza, Clouds, and Katanas
content: A yakuza-inspired gang with bosozoku biker roots that dominates Japantown, Charter Hill, and parts of Watson under Arasaka's quiet protective umbrella. They run dollhouses like Clouds, casinos, slot parlors, and brutal illegal braindance networks like Jotaro Shobo's. In combat, they favor fast katanas, Sandevistans, and SMGs.

title: The Tyger Claws' Smart-Targeting Jammer Tattoo
content: Critical tactical advantage against the Tyger Claws: most members wear a dermal photoluminescent circuit tattoo—gifted by Wakako Okada or Arasaka—that emits electromagnetic countermeasures capable of scrambling Smart weapon micro-projectiles mid-flight. Against them, stick to Power weapons, Tech weapons, or quickhacks.

title: The Valentinos — Honor, Gold, and Heywood Chicano Culture
content: Rooted in the 2020s and deeply tied to Heywood's Latino community, the Valentinos flaunt chromed-out rides, Liberty firearms and gold-plated pistols, and fierce devotion to Santa Muerte. They value family, keeping one's word, and neighborhood pride, maintaining solid ties with local residents and Padre Ibarra.

title: 6th Street — Militarized Veterans of Santo Domingo
content: Formed by Fourth Corporate War veterans to defend Santo Domingo when the NCPD abandoned the suburbs, 6th Street degenerated into a gun-running extortion militia after Will Gunner's bloody internal coup against its moderate founders. They wear surplus military camo and stockpile smuggled automatic and Smart weapons.

title: Voodoo Boys — Insular Creole Netrunners of Coastview
content: After climate disasters sank Haiti in 2062, its survivors fortified themselves in Coastview, Pacifica, building a self-reliant community led by elite netrunners like Maman Brigitte and her lieutenant Placide. They treat every outsider as disposable—calling them "ranyon"—and dream of striking a pact with the AIs beyond the Blackwall.

title: The Animals — Hyper-Musculature, Juice, and Brute Force
content: A gang obsessed with pushing the human physique past its limits using mutagenic veterinary serum ("Juice"), armored subdermal plating, and Gorilla Arms. They work as nightclub bouncers, underground boxing champions like Rhino, and shock mercs; their deadliest pack fortified the GIM shopping mall under Sasquatch.

title: Scavengers (Scavs) — Kidnapping and Cyberware Harvesting
content: The most despised faction in Night City, reviled even by other gangs. Scattered cells—many made up of former Soviet exiles—abduct civilians and careless mercs to butcher them in ice baths, strip out every usable piece of warm chrome, and fence it on underground markets while hiding behind holo-pixelated face masks.

title: The Mox (Moxes) — Defenders of Lizzie's Bar After Elizabeth Borden's Death
content: Founded in 2076 after the brutal murder of Lizzie Borden—a club owner who protected her girls—at the hands of the Tyger Claws. Also known as the Moxes, they turned Lizzie's Bar in Kabuki into their headquarters, operating under Suzie Q's pragmatic leadership as a close-quarters shield against pimps and abusive gangs.

title: Barghest — Colonel Kurt Hansen's Private Army in Dogtown
content: A former Militech strike unit that refused to pull out after the 2070 Arvin Accord, digging in alongside Colonel Kurt Hansen behind Dogtown's stadium walls. They control arms smuggling and supply airdrops under their own martial law, patrolling the streets in heavy armor and military bots.

title: The Aldecaldos — The Nomad Clan of Saul, Panam, Mitch, and Scorpion
content: One of the seven great Nomad Nations of North America, the Bright family of the Aldecaldos camps in the Badlands outside Night City. Unification War veterans like Mitch and Scorpion repair heavy machinery and escort convoys—torn in 2077 between signing a Biotechnica contract for survival or reclaiming their independent pride.

title: The Wraiths (Raffen Shiv) and the Disbanded Bakkers Clan
content: Under Nomad law, anyone who betrays their clan is branded Raffen Shiv: banished scum who band together into violent packs like the Wraiths in the Badlands to raid convoys, torture prisoners, and fence stolen cyberware. By contrast, many wandering former Bakkers ended up absorbed into the corporate-backed Snake Nation.

title: Afterlife Mercs, The Inquisitors, and Minor Sects of Night City
content: Beyond the major turf gangs, notorious cells and extremist sects persist in Night City's history: anti-cyberware zealots descended from the Inquisitors, sadistic cyborg-clowns carrying on the legacy of the Bozos (like the explosive Ozob Bozo in 2077), and the occult cyber-cult within Maelstrom dabbling in rituals from beyond the Blackwall.
